Cautious but policy-backstopped. The statement underscores pandemic-driven downside risks to activity, employment, and inflation, yet it pairs these with strong accommodation: a 0–1/4 percent policy rate, sizable Treasury/MBS purchases, and outcome-based forward guidance under the Fed’s average-inflation-targeting “makeup” strategy (as announced by Chair Powell at Jackson Hole 2020). Academic work suggests such frameworks help anchor expectations—see inflation-forecast targeting in Svensson and Woodford (2005)—and that at the zero lower bound, forward guidance and QE work through expectations and term-premium channels to ease financial conditions (Curdia and Woodford, 2008; Bernanke and coauthors; Cochrane–Piazzesi on the term structure). The willingness to let inflation moderately overshoot 2 percent is consistent with the Taylor principle emphasis in Clarida’s research and supports re-anchoring inflation expectations. Taken together, the communication is risk-aware but tempered by credible, literature-consistent tools that mitigate the negative tone.
